headline: Suki, a company whose AI tools write doctors' clinical notes from recorded visits, has raised $90 million to build AI agents for follow-up tasks such as referrals and prior authorisations.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a mid-sized health AI funding round, announced by the company, in a crowded field.
importance_line: Clinicians and patients could see AI take over paperwork such as referrals and insurer approvals if the new agents work, and Suki's partners such as athenahealth and Zoom could get more built-in features, but the agents are plans, not products, the revenue figures are Suki's own, and better-funded rivals compete hard.
summary: Healthcare Dive reports that Suki, whose software for doctors includes ambient listening (recording a visit and writing the clinical note automatically), order entry and billing-code suggestions, has raised $90 million in a Series E round, with new investors Healthier Capital, Crosslink Capital and Hercules Capital joining existing backers, and will spend it on AI agents for tasks after a visit such as referrals and prior authorisations (insurer approvals for treatments or drugs) and on deepening ties with the more than 30 technology partners that embed its tools. Suki's founder and chief executive, Punit Soni, says raising rounds of $100 million or more can create unreasonably high expectations, in a market where rivals Ambience Healthcare raised $243 million and Abridge $300 million last year; Suki's own release says its revenue doubled in 2025 and is on track to do so again in 2026.
notes: Read in full via fulltext (the saved text lacks the first paragraph); the Suki Business Wire release on Yahoo Finance supplied investor names, revenue claim and Soni's title.
